Laura / team —

Attached is a draft subject-line test matrix and the proposed 3-email invite cadence. Key notes:
- Subject lines (A/B/C):
  A) "How to cut LLM inference cost without sacrificing latency" (brand-forward)
  B) "Reduce inference spend: proven techniques from Scale-ups" (value-forward)
  C) "Live: Model serving tactics that drop per-token cost" (curiosity-forward)
- Cadence options:
  Light: Invite (3 days out), Reminder (1 day out), Day-of reminder (1 hour)
  Heavy: Invite (7 days out), Reminder (3 days out), Reminder (1 day out), Day-of reminder (2 hours)
- I recommend variant mapping: EdgeScale list => subject A/B; Redwood warm eng => subject B/C.

I've attached subject-line-tests.xlsx and a short copy deck. Also included proposed preheader options and 2 snippet variants for preview panes.

If that looks good I'll create HubSpot smart lists for each segment and hand off to Ops for link insertion.

—Marissa

Nice matrix — a couple of tracking asks from growth:
- UTM convention: utm_source={partner|redwood}, utm_medium=email, utm_campaign=redwood_edgescale_jul27, utm_content={subject_variant}_{segment}
- Use unique HubSpot query params so we can attribute registrations back to the smart list (hs_campaign=HS-2027-0711 + hs_list=EDGE_WARM_1 etc.)
- For calendar deeplinks, generate both Google Calendar and ICS/Outlook links; also include a universal deep link for mobile (calshow:// or webcal:// fallback).

I added a small tracking-link-map.md stub in Drive — Hannah, can you QA the mapping and make sure the landing page accepts the utm/hs params so the registrant record surfaces correctly in HubSpot?

—Vivek
